# Body lift installation tips and tricks

## Summary

[Partial] Disconnect wire harness, modify brake line bracket, address ABS lines, loosen upper radiator hose, and remove rear bumper. [t755]

[Partial] Remove the brake line bracket in the driver wheel well using two bolts. [t755]

Disconnect the ABS lines in both wheel wells. [t755]

Remove the steering box arm located inside the cab. [t755]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Disconnect the wire harness located in the passenger wheel well.
2. Remove or modify the brake line bracket found on the driver side wheel well (two bolts).
3. [Partial] Address ABS lines running through both front and rear wheel wells as needed.
4. [Partial] Disconnect the steering box arm inside the cab to clear space for one bolt's worth of movement.
5. Loosen and disconnect the upper radiator hose to prevent cracking the neck during lifting.
6. [Partial] Remove, reposition, and reinstall the rear bumper if it interferes with clearance.

_Procedure reported by [t755]._

## Tips & gotchas

- Extend the power steering hoses instead of cutting or notching the bracket for easier installation. [t755]
- Use a longer upper radiator hose rather than risking cracks on the original neck. [t755]
- Extend power steering hoses instead of modifying brackets for easier installation. [t755]
- Use a longer radiator hose to avoid cracking the neck during removal and reinstallation. [t755]
